newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower on trade selling.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower on trade selling.

text.p: COMEX copper ended lower Monday largely on commercial hedge selling capped by fund buying at the bottom of the range.
Copper took a back seat to the other base metals, namely zinc, nickel and aluminum, all of which rallied on strong technical buying, brokers said.
The active September contract closed at 109.70 cents a lb, down 1.75 cents from Friday's close, while the spot month fell 112.80 cents a lb, down 1.20 cents.
"We saw some producer selling," said Frederick Demler, minerals economist with ED&F Man. "We were in an overbought position. So it wasn't too surprising to see us weaker on the day.
"The funds were buyers below the close. That coupled with the strong day in zinc, nickel and aluminum, provided some support for the market," he added.

The London Metal Exchange warehouse stocks increased another 3,900 tonnes to 214,125 tonnes, continuing a six-week trend of higher stocks. The increases came from the Singapore and European warehouses, reflecting the weaker demand in those regions, dealers said.

COMEX warehouse stocks showed its first increase since July 1, indicating a shift in the arbitrage from as much as a 6.50-cent LME cash premium two weeks ago to a 3.25-cent COMEX premium at Monday's close.

"Previously we could claim that the LME warehouse increase was the result of arbitrage shipments from COMEX warehouses," one dealer said. "Now that's no longer the case. We have to think it's a function of weak demand in Europe and Asia."
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
